Stated Claim / Post Context:
GOP set to lose the House in midterms 'massacre' as country turns on Trump: Live updates

Donald Trump was staring down an election-night nightmare on Tuesday as Democrats surged toward taking control of the House of Representatives.

Actual Article Body:
By BREANNE DEPPISCH, US SENIOR POLITICAL REPORTER and RACHEL BOWMAN, US SENIOR NEWS REPORTER and JON MICHAEL RAASCH, WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT and VICTOR HELLER, US REPORTER and VICTORIA CHURCHILL, US POLITICAL REPORTER

Updated:  14:36 AEDT, 4 November 2026

Donald Trump is staring down an electoral nightmare after Democrats surged toward taking control of the House of Representatives in a crushing blow that threatens to cripple the final two years of his presidency.

Republicans were bracing for a feared 'blue tsunami' as the Democrats also claimed the first major Senate battleground of the night, with former North Carolina governor Roy Cooper snatching a crucial seat from GOP hands.

The victory turned the Tar Heel state blue and delivered another ominous warning to Trump as his party fights to stave off a devastating midterm defeat.

In yet another GOP upset, Democrat Senate candidate Annie Andrews won the US Senate election in South Carolina, beating out Darline Graham, the sister of the late Senator Lindsey Graham.

In the Senate, Democrats must flip four Republican-held seats to gain control. In the House, they need to pick up just three seats.

Americans turned out in droves to make their voices heard on a slew of issues, including the cost of living and the war in Iran, while chaos erupted in several key battleground states.

The first polls closed at 6pm ET and the last polls wrap up at 1am ET. Then the nation will wait as ballots are counted across the country to find out whether Republicans or Democrats will take power.

Follow the Daily Mail for more updates...

Daily Mail columnist Mark Halperin said Republican strategists believe the midterm elections are going to be catastrophic for the GOP.

One person told him: 'There will be surprise winners and surprise survivors, but it's going to be a bloodbath.'

Another said: 'This is going to be a massacre. Donald Trump asked voters to vote as if he was on the ballot. They did.'

Fox News anchor Sean Hannity spoke after Democrat Annie Andrews was announced as the shock winner of South Carolina's Senate race, flipping the seat blue for the first time in more than 20 years.

'It's sad to me,' Hannity said. 'It ended tragically.'

California Representative Robert Garcia is the ranking member of the House Oversight Committee and will become chairman after Democrats secured the majority tonight.

He released a blunt message to Republicans after the Democrats' majority was projected.

'Lawyer up,' Garcia said.

Senator Susan Collins's watch party had thinned out by 10pm, two hours after she first delivered remarks and the polls closed.

The incumbent is running for her sixth term against Democratic challenger Troy Jackson and spoke briefly at 8pm, thanking the crowd and noting the results were too early to call. After her remarks, she disappeared to a side room.

Around 9.45pm, Collins re-emerged to shake hands, take pictures and thank her supporters.

Those who remained gripped their drinks nervously as they watched Fox News and waited for results to trickle in.

Many others had migrated to the hotel's bar just outside the conference room, where they continued following the results.

Outside, a light drizzle seemed to mirror the subdued mood inside.

Democratic nominee Zach Dembo has won Kentucky's Sixth House District against Republican rival Ralph Alvarado.

Dembo has flipped the seat that GOP incumbent Andy Barr won in 2024 by 26.1 percentage points.

AP called the race at 10.16pm.

It's the second race the AP has called where Democrats have flipped a Republican-held seat. They just need one more to win control of the House.

NBC News chief data analyst Steve Kornacki was stunned when his network announced the South Carolina Senate race was leaning towards Annie Andrews.

'Yeah, a really big surprise here, I think, puts Darline Graham in a tough spot here in South Carolina. This is shocking,' he said.

'I don't want to say catastrophic because it's only declared a lean right now, but if you’re Graham, those are very scary numbers for you.'

The network projected Andrews's win shortly after.

As Texas Democratic Senate hopeful James Talarico's supporters waited for major networks to call his own race, they cheered, cheers-ed - with tallboys of Love Street Blonde - and embraced over the news that the Democrats have won back the House of Representatives.

Talarico and Texas Democratic gubernatorial hopeful Gina Hinojosa were leading their Republican rivals, though neither race has been called.

A New York State Supreme Court judge has issued a consent order, supported by both Republicans and Democrats, on how ballots will be counted in Westchester County, CNN reported.

The filing states how unscanned ballots will be collected, secured and counted after issues were reported with voting machines at multiple polling stations.

The final count will determine the winner of the House race between incumbent Republican Representative Mike Lawler and Democrat Cait Conley.

Democrat Senate candidate Annie Andrews won the US Senate election in South Carolina, beating out Darline Graham, the sister of the late Senator Lindsey Graham.

Trump endorsed Darline to replace her brother after he died unexpectedly in July.

CNN and NBC News called the race before 10.05pm. The Associated Press reported a 51 percent advantage for Andrews, with 87 percent of votes counted.

The flip is another major shock for Republicans. Lindsey Graham won the seat in 2020 by ten percentage points. The seat hasn't been held by a Democrat in 28 years.

Explore more

Darline Graham loses late brother Lindsey's South Carolina Senate seat

Darline Graham has been defeated by Democrat Annie Andrews in South Carolina, dealing a stinging blow to Donald Trump.

Senator Jon Ossoff struck a defiant tone in his victory speech, declaring that while Democrats had plenty to celebrate, the fight to address America's deeper problems is far from over.

'The underlying crisis gripping our republic remains, and that therefore, our most vital work lies ahead,' Ossoff said.

Ossoff said the political system was still working for the wealthy and powerful while everyday Americans struggle to keep up with rising costs and healthcare bills.

He also vowed to keep taking on big pharma, insurance companies and big tech, saying they needed to be held accountable.

Jon Ossoff romps to victory in Georgia as victory fuels 2028 talk

Georgia Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff has won re-election in Georgia, defeating Republican challenger Mike Collins after a brutal race.
